pages.title: System
pages.intro: Is this PC running well – and what has changed?

tabsDetail.label: Services
tipTexts: Every service needs its own “door number” (port). If another program uses it or two services want the same one, one cannot start. “Change port” gives a stopped service a port that is really free – a specific one if you like. Right-click a row for more.
Port overview Everything it could do is here. You no longer need the extension – removing it is safe, Hostwerk services and ports stay unchanged.

tabsDetail.label: Performance
tipTexts: Disk and network Disk: Windows counts all input and output of the program here – files, but also network and devices. Network: needs administrator rights on Windows – set it up once with “Measure network”.

tabsDetail.label: Storage
tipTexts: Check regularly with admin rights Hostwerk sets up a Windows task that reads the values every hour with administrator rights. Windows asks for permission once. The task only reads and removes itself when you uninstall the extension.

Why administrator rights? Without administrator rights Windows only shows whether a drive is healthy. Temperature, wear and error counters are read in a single check – Windows asks for permission once. Hostwerk itself keeps running without admin rights.
Notifications Warnings go to Hostwerk’s notifications (push, Discord, ntfy, mail) and appear under Go live → Monitoring → Watchers.

tabsDetail.label: Maintenance
areas: What Hostwerk takes care of by itself
actions: Open area: Certificates (Let’s Encrypt, local CA)
Open area: AI programs and models
Open area: Docker engine and images
Open area: Router port forwards & DynDNS
Open area: End of life of versions
tipTexts: Hostwerk keeps itself up to date without a new version: updates of other programs only go live after a trial run, on errors the last working version stays. If a download source disappears, Hostwerk takes a replacement source. “Check everything now” starts all checks right away (up to a minute) – otherwise they run on schedule.

Per task: whether it currently runs by itself, when something last happened and roughly when next. The switch is the same as in the settings. The ⓘ per row explains what exactly happens and what you can do yourself.

Hostwerk itself New versions are downloaded in the background and become active on the next start (incl. runtime). Hostwerk checks daily for new versions, downloads them in the background and swaps them on the next start. If the new version doesn’t start cleanly, the previous one keeps running automatically. What you can do: Nothing – unless you want to skip versions (Settings → Updates).

PHP (patch versions) Security updates with a trial run and rollback. Every 6 hours Hostwerk looks for security updates within your PHP series (e.g. 8.3.x). The new version is installed next to the old one, tested with a trial run and only then activated. If the test fails, the old one stays. What you can do: You decide on bigger jumps (8.3 → 8.4) yourself – Hostwerk only suggests them.

Databases (patch versions) Security updates with a trial run and rollback. Like PHP: patch versions of MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL are checked, installed with a trial run and rolled back on errors. What you can do: You switch major versions yourself in the database area.

Web servers (patch versions) Security updates with a trial run. Apache, nginx and Caddy get security updates within their series – with a trial run; the old version stays as a way back. What you can do: Nothing.

Certificates (Let’s Encrypt, local CA) Renewed after 1/3 of the lifetime or on expiry. HTTPS certificates (Let’s Encrypt and Hostwerk’s local certificate authority) are renewed in time. What you can do: Nothing – Hostwerk reports any error.

AI programs and models Ollama, sd.cpp, whisper, Pocket TTS and models with a trial run; catalogs daily. Ollama, image models, speech recognition and voices are updated with a trial run; the model catalogs arrive online daily. What you can do: If AI is turned off, there is nothing to do here.
Runtime (Node/Electron) Self-test before swapping, rollback on error. Node.js and Electron, which Hostwerk runs on, are swapped with the app update – after a self-test. What you can do: Nothing.

Restore test Test-restore every 7 days. The latest backup is regularly restored into a throwaway environment and checked. That way a broken backup is noticed before you need it. What you can do: Nothing.

Health check Monthly report on all computers with workflow suggestions. A report on all computers: services, backups, certificates, storage, OS updates – with a score and suggestions. What you can do: Turn on the schedule (daily, weekly or monthly) or use “Check now” when needed.

Cleanup (leftovers, cache, trash) Daily: installation leftovers, old downloads, trash after 30 days. Hostwerk cleans up installation leftovers and old downloads daily; the trash is emptied after 30 days. What you can do: Nothing.

tabsDetail.label: Changes
tipTexts: Every change to services, shares and settings – whether in the app, via remote access, from another computer, the AI or a task. Entries with “Undo” can be reverted one by one. The camera icon marks a state you can return to under Backups → Restore. Kept for 90 days.

tipTexts: Themes from extensions A theme changes colours, font, rounding and spacing – only through checked values. Hostwerk only applies it if texts and controls stay easy to read (WCAG 2.2 AA). If the extension is removed, Hostwerk’s own look returns.
Accent color Color for buttons, marks and highlights – you see it everywhere right away. Extensions adopt it. With custom colors Hostwerk adjusts buttons and text so everything stays readable.
Interface zoom Makes text and controls larger or smaller everywhere – up to 200 % without cutting anything off. Applies wherever you open Hostwerk – in the browser and on your phone too.
Your name Stays in the settings on this computer – not in setup files, exports or logs; error reports replace it with “<name>”. It is only used where you turn it on below.

tipTexts: “Stable” only gets finished versions, and new versions arrive step by step – first for a few, then for everyone. “Preview” also gets test versions right away as soon as they appear. Small updates within the same version (e.g. PHP 8.4.11 → 8.4.12). Hostwerk downloads the new version next to the old one, switches over and quickly checks that everything runs. If it doesn’t, the old version stays active. Hostwerk never makes big version jumps on its own.

pages.title: Hostwerk network
pages.intro: More PCs and servers with Hostwerk – operate all of them from here, move projects and game servers, put backups back.
tipTexts: How it works Install Hostwerk on the other machine (Windows or Linux; a rented server works with “Own server with one click”), switch on remote access there and enter the pairing code here. Then switch between the devices in the machine bar at the top – services, files, terminal and AI then run on the chosen machine. Linux servers in a data centre · Windows or Linux PCs at home · Phone: under Go live → Access → Remote access

Rented server (e.g. at Hetzner, Netcup, IONOS) or a home server with Ubuntu, Debian or Fedora: Hostwerk sets itself up there – Node.js, Hostwerk without a window as a service, remote access with two-factor, firewall – and then shows up here as a machine. Your SSH sign-in is only used for the setup and never stored.
Another Hostwerk PC can then operate this machine – through remote access (HTTPS) with its own key that you can revoke at any time. The key is shown only once.

pages.title: Discord control
pages.intro: Your own Discord bot: /status, /players, /start, /stop and /restart from your Discord server.
tipTexts: Commands /status – which services run · /players – who is online · /start, /stop, /restart <service> – with a confirm button for stop and restart. German Discord shows /spieler and /neustart.
Your own bot The bot belongs to you: Hostwerk logs in with your token, the token stays encrypted on this PC and only goes to Discord.

How to get the token Open the Discord developer portal and create a “New Application” – its name is what people see in Discord, for example “Hostwerk”. Under “Bot” click “Reset Token” and copy the token. No special intents are needed. Paste the token here.

Rights Everyone on your Discord server may use /status and /players. Starting, stopping and restarting is only for the roles chosen here, server admins (if allowed) and linked team members – for exactly the services shared with them in the Team extension.
Shared services Only these appear in /status and can be started or stopped from Discord. Others stay invisible there – even for admins.

pages.title: Discord status
pages.intro: Shows “Playing Hostwerk” in your Discord profile – even when Hostwerk only runs in the tray.
tipTexts: What is shared? Only kinds of services (for example web server · database) and how many are running. Never project or folder names – a server name only if you switch it on.

pages.title: Drives
pages.intro: How healthy and how full your drives are – checked regularly.
tipTexts: Drives Hostwerk reads the S.M.A.R.T. values of every drive – temperature, wear, errors – and tells you when something gets worse, and shows how full the drive is and who uses the space. Nothing on a drive is ever changed.

Check regularly with admin rights Hostwerk sets up a Windows task that reads the values every hour with administrator rights. Windows asks for permission once. The task only reads and removes itself when you uninstall the extension.

Why administrator rights? Without administrator rights Windows only shows whether a drive is healthy. Temperature, wear and error counters are read in a single check – Windows asks for permission once. Hostwerk itself keeps running without admin rights.
Notifications Warnings go to Hostwerk’s notifications (push, Discord, ntfy, mail) and appear under Go live → Monitoring → Watchers.

pages.title: Storage per service
pages.intro: Space used per service and free space on the drive.
actions: From the extension “Storage per service” – info

pages.title: DNS → Names
pages.intro: Names for this connection – free or with your own domain – and all records at your provider, kept up to date by themselves.
tipTexts: This connection The address the internet sees. Hostwerk asks several services (no account needed) and only trusts an address two of them agree on. For IPv6 it uses this PC’s fixed address, not the changing privacy address.

Maintenance-free Every 5 minutes Hostwerk checks the address and updates a name only when it changed. Every 6 hours it checks that the world really sees this connection. Problems come as one notification; a provider that is down is retried with growing pauses.

tabsDetail.label: Providers
tipTexts: Mail server records MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC from the extension “Mail server”. Records that are missing at your provider are set with one click; existing SPF/DMARC records are replaced, nothing else is touched.

pages.title: File share
pages.intro: Share a folder over SFTP or as a download link – for worlds, mods or photos.
tipTexts: Fingerprint On the first connection the SFTP program shows this fingerprint. If it is the same, the connection really goes to this PC.
Router Windows may ask once whether Hostwerk may receive connections – allow it for private networks.

pages.title: Knowledge graph → Graph
pages.intro: Code, docs and notes as a graph – ask questions, see connections, connect Claude and forget it again.

pages.title: Mail statistics
pages.intro: How many e-mails your projects send – per day, per project, per sender and recipient. Data from the mail catcher.

pages.title: Minecraft server network
pages.intro: Several servers behind one address, Java and Bedrock together – kept up to date by itself.
tipTexts: How it fits together A proxy (Velocity) is the one address players connect to; it sends them to your servers and lets them switch with /server. Geyser on the proxy translates for Bedrock players (phone, console, Windows), Floodgate lets them in without a Java account. ViaVersion lets other Minecraft versions in. A Bedrock Dedicated Server is something else: Mojang’s own server with a separate Bedrock-only world.

pages.title: Page check
pages.intro: How fast is the page, what do search engines see, can everyone use it and is it safe? With concrete tips.
tipTexts: Regular checks Hostwerk checks these addresses on its own and tells you when the score drops by 5 points or more.
Minimum score Publishing extensions (e.g. “Publish pages”) check the page first and stop below this score. 0 = off.

pages.title: Leaderboard → Leaderboard
pages.intro: Who plays, mines, kills or dies the most – across all Minecraft servers or per server, all time or for the week and month, with player search, profile card, badges and history. Right in the “Players” tab of every Minecraft server, as a stream view for OBS and, if you like, as an own web page in your web server.

pages.title: Players → Live
pages.intro: Who is playing right now and who plays the most – across all Minecraft and game servers.

pages.title: Ports
pages.intro: Now built into Hostwerk (System → Services → Ports & services). All ports of your services in one list: what runs, what another program blocks, where two services want the same port, what the router forwards – “change port” with one click, a free check and free suggestions to copy.

pages.title: Profiler
pages.intro: Find out why a page or app is slow – which functions and database queries take the time.

pages.title: Quick tasks
pages.intro: Your tasks as big buttons – one click runs a backup, a report or a script (Hostwerk asks first). Pin favourites, also as a tile.

pages.title: Router & port forwarding
pages.intro: Reach your servers from the internet: forwardings, IPv6, DynDNS and – after signing in – devices and Wi-Fi of your router.
tipTexts: Forward automatically Hostwerk forwards the ports of your public services (websites with a domain, Minecraft, mail server, remote access) in the router and keeps them up to date – also after new servers or changed ports.
Manage forwardings automatically Checks every 30 minutes and after the start; cleans up Hostwerk forwardings that are no longer needed.

Tip for FRITZ!Box On the FRITZ!Box under Internet → Permit Access → Port Sharing, switch on "Permit independent port sharing for this device" for this PC. Otherwise it refuses automatic forwardings. Open router

pages.title: Schematics in 3D
pages.intro: Look at Minecraft builds before you place them – from WorldEdit, Litematica, MCEdit and structure blocks.
tipTexts: Where do the files come from? Hostwerk looks through the folders of your Minecraft servers (for example plugins/WorldEdit/schematics, schematics/ or structures/). Any build file in the file browser opens in 3D as well.

pages.title: Notes → Checklist
pages.intro: All notes about your services – with search and checklists you can tick off.

pages.title: Publish static sites
pages.intro: Put a project online with one click – on GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Codeberg Pages or your own server.

pages.title: Team & roles → Users
pages.intro: Let friends and colleagues in – each with their own sign-in and only the rights they need.
tipTexts: How roles work Every person signs in to remote access with their own name and password (or passkey). Members only see and control the services and areas you share – for example “start the survival server and manage players”. The change log shows who did what.

tabsDetail.label: Activity
tipTexts: Activity What members changed (from Hostwerk's change log) and what they tried without permission. Refused attempts are kept here – the last 200.

tabsDetail.label: Team setup
tipTexts: What is a team setup? One shared setup for everyone in the team: it lives in a shared folder (OneDrive, network drive, Git repository) or at an address. Hostwerk checks every 15 minutes for changes and asks before taking anything over – it only adds what is missing.

pages.title: Uptime wall → Wall
pages.intro: Uptime of all monitors at a glance.

pages.title: Visitor stats
pages.intro: Visitors of your sites – from the web server logs, without cookies.
tipTexts: Privacy No cookies, no fingerprint. IP addresses are shortened (the last part removed) and turned into a hash that changes every day – after two days not even this PC can link visits. Bots, crawlers, uptime checks, images and scripts are left out. Nothing leaves this PC.

pages.title: VPN
pages.intro: Reach this PC from anywhere – one port forwarding instead of many, everything else stays private.
tipTexts: WireGuard is missing You can already create accesses – the configurations work as soon as the tunnel runs.

pages.title: Vulnerabilities
pages.intro: Known vulnerabilities of everything Hostwerk runs – matched to the installed version, ordered by severity.
actions: High 8.4 A flaw in Node.js Permission Model enforcement can over-grant filesystem access across radix-tree prefix boundaries. CVE-2026-58043
tipTexts: Act now There are critical or actively exploited vulnerabilities.

Sources Free databases without a key: OSV.dev, the NVD (by CPE), CISA’s list of exploited vulnerabilities and FIRST’s EPSS. Hostwerk asks once a day, bundled and throttled, and keeps the answers – if a source is down, the last state stays. New critical or exploited findings go to Hostwerk’s notifications (Settings → Notifications).

pages.title: Webhook inbox
pages.intro: Receive webhooks from Stripe, GitHub & co., look inside, check signatures and pass them on to your project.
